topic: Primary tumor (GTV) and lymph node AI in head & neck cancer on CT and PET/CT - HECKTOR 2021-2025, CT-only GTV segmentation, lymph node detection and automatic Robbins level classification, radiologic ENE, HPV-from-CT, tumor volumetrics, depth of invasion

findings.title: HEad and neCK TumOR (HECKTOR) 2025: Benchmark of Segmentation, Diagnosis, and Prognosis in Multimodal PET/CT
findings.summary: Latest HECKTOR edition: three tasks - GTVp+GTVn segmentation, recurrence-free survival, HPV status - on >1100 patients from 10 centers, now including RT dose maps. 35 teams, 15 final submissions. Top results: mean Dice 0.75 (segmentation), C-index 0.66 (RFS), balanced accuracy 0.56 (HPV).
findings.relevance: Sets the realistic ceiling for Margin's auto-GTV / auto-node feature, and is the single strongest argument that HPV-from-CT must NOT ship as a clinical readout (0.56 balanced accuracy = near chance).
findings.license: arXiv open access (paper); data under challenge DUA
findings.feasibility: Reference only, no inference cost.

findings.title: HECKTOR 2025 Grand Challenge - tasks and evaluation
findings.summary: Official task definitions and metrics (aggregated Dice for GTVp/GTVn, C-index, balanced accuracy). Training data - FDG-PET/CT volumes, GTVp/GTVn masks, clinical CSV - downloadable after registration and a data use agreement.
findings.relevance: Most realistic source of labelled H&N GTVp/GTVn pairs for validating anything Margin ships, and a ready supply of real PET/CT test cases for the Cornerstone3D viewer and the pydicom ingest path.
findings.license: Challenge data use agreement, non-commercial research; registration required
findings.feasibility: Download only. NIfTI/DICOM - pydicom + SimpleITK read directly. No GPU.

findings.title: Overview of the HECKTOR Challenge at MICCAI 2021: Automatic Head and Neck Tumor Segmentation and Outcome Prediction in PET/CT Images
findings.summary: HECKTOR 2021: Task 1 GTVp segmentation on FDG-PET/CT (oropharynx), Task 2 progression-free survival, Task 3 both. Best GTVp Dice ~0.779. Established the PET+CT two-channel input convention and the fixed bounding-box crop around the oropharynx that most later methods reuse.
findings.relevance: Documents the preprocessing recipe (resample to ~1 mm isotropic, 144^3 crop, PET SUV normalization) Margin's FastAPI/SimpleITK preprocessing layer must replicate for any HECKTOR-derived model to work.
findings.license: arXiv open access
findings.feasibility: Preprocessing itself is trivially CPU-feasible in SimpleITK (seconds).

findings.title: Automated head and neck tumor segmentation from 3D PET/CT (NVAUTO - HECKTOR 2022 winner, SegResNet via MONAI Auto3DSeg)
findings.summary: Winning HECKTOR 2022 solution: MONAI SegResNet trained with Auto3DSeg, resample to common resolution, crop the head-and-neck region, 5-fold CV, ensemble of 15 models from 3 runs. Aggregated Dice 0.78802 (1st place) over GTVp + GTVn.
findings.relevance: SegResNet is the best-documented architecture for joint GTVp/GTVn. MONAI is pip-installable and CPU-capable, so a single-fold SegResNet is the most plausible tumor model Margin could actually ship locally.
findings.license: MONAI / Auto3DSeg code is Apache-2.0; the challenge-winning weights were NOT publicly released - retraining or a substitute checkpoint is required
findings.feasibility: MONAI + CPU torch pip-install cleanly at Windows user level (proxy: set PIP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY). One SegResNet forward pass on a 144^3 crop is ~10-60 s on CPU; the 15-model ensemble is not feasible - use 1 fold, sliding-window with small overlap.

findings.title: HNLNL_autosegmentation_trained_models - trained nnU-Net models for head & neck lymph node LEVEL autosegmentation
findings.summary: Publicly released nnU-Net 3D-fullres/2D ensemble weights (in the Releases tab) that segment 20 separate head & neck lymph node LEVELS on CT, plus 'Adjust3DCNNcontoursToCTslicePlaneOrientation.py', a 3D Slicer post-processing module that snaps contours to the CT slice plane. Repository license is CC0-1.0 (public domain dedication), confirmed on the repo page.
findings.relevance: The highest-value asset in this whole search for Margin. Run it once per neck CT to get 20 level masks, then assign any detected/clicked node to a Robbins level by mask overlap or centroid containment - no hand-coded anatomic rules, no atlas registration. Also lets the viewer overlay level boundaries for teaching and op-note dictation.
findings.license: CC0-1.0 on the repository (verify the same applies to the release binaries before distributing them inside Margin; nnU-Net itself is Apache-2.0)
findings.feasibility: nnU-Net pip-installs on Windows at user level with CPU-only torch. 3D-fullres CPU inference on a neck CT is slow - expect several minutes to ~15 min per case with TTA disabled (--disable_tta) and a single fold; 32 GB RAM is ample. Run it as a background FastAPI job, cache the level masks per study.

findings.title: Deep learning for automatic head and neck lymph node level delineation provides expert-level accuracy
findings.summary: Methods paper for the released weights. 35 expert-delineated planning CTs for training, 20 for test; nnU-Net 3D-fullres/2D ensemble over 20 nodal levels. Slice-plane-adjusted DL contours were rated significantly better than unadjusted, and geometric accuracy was not different from intraobserver variability.
findings.relevance: Gives the exact level nomenclature/label indices Margin must map to Robbins/Gregoire names, and justifies implementing the slice-plane adjustment step in the FastAPI post-processing rather than shipping raw model output.
findings.license: Open access (PMC)
findings.feasibility: Slice-adjustment logic is plain numpy - CPU trivial. Reimplement it in the backend rather than depending on 3D Slicer.

findings.title: Deep Learning and Registration-Based Mapping for Analyzing the Distribution of Nodal Metastases in Head and Neck Cancer Cohorts
findings.venue_or_repo: PMC10526893 (Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys / Adv Radiat Oncol)
findings.summary: Combines lymph node level autosegmentation with deformable registration to a reference frame to automatically assign nodal metastases to 20 head & neck nodal levels; correctly categorized all 449 nodes in a cohort of 193 head and neck cancer patients.
findings.relevance: The published blueprint for Margin's 'which Robbins level is this node in?' feature - specifically the node-centroid-in-level-mask assignment logic layered on top of level segmentations, and how to handle nodes straddling two levels.
findings.license: Open access (PMC)
findings.feasibility: Assignment logic is pure numpy/SimpleITK label overlap - milliseconds on CPU. Avoid the deformable-registration variant (SimpleITK demons/BSpline on a neck CT is minutes on CPU); go direct-segmentation instead.

findings.title: Delineation of the neck node levels for head and neck tumors: a 2013 update - DAHANCA, EORTC, HKNPCSG, NCIC CTG, NCRI, RTOG, TROG consensus guidelines (Gregoire et al.)
findings.summary: The consensus CT-based nodal atlas: 10 node groups, several subdivided into levels, each with explicit cranial/caudal/anterior/posterior/lateral/medial boundaries keyed to CT landmarks, plus the primary sites at risk for each level. Supersedes the 2003 N0-neck guidelines (PMID 14644481).
findings.relevance: Ground truth for Margin's level definitions and for the human-readable boundary text displayed next to an auto-assigned level; also the fallback rule set if we ever implement landmark-based level assignment (using TotalSegmentator hyoid/cricoid/carotid/SCM landmarks) instead of a DL model.
findings.license: Copyrighted guideline - link and cite; do not embed verbatim text in the app
findings.feasibility: No compute. Boundary rules encodable as landmark-relative geometry.

findings.title: Multi-Institutional Validation of Deep Learning for Pretreatment Identification of Extranodal Extension in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Kann et al.)
findings.summary: 3D CNN on annotated lymph nodes from pretreatment CT. External institution: AUC 0.84, accuracy 83.1%, versus radiologist AUCs 0.70 and 0.71. TCGA set: AUC 0.90, accuracy 88.6%, versus radiologist AUCs 0.60 and 0.82. The reference multi-institutional ENE result.
findings.relevance: Benchmark for a Margin 'radiologic ENE risk' flag on a user-clicked node. Important caveat for the UI: the model consumes a node-centered crop, so it depends on Margin first localizing the node.
findings.license: Paywalled paper; no public weights or code found in this search
findings.feasibility: Architecture is a small 3D CNN on a node-centered patch - CPU inference would be sub-second IF weights existed. They do not; retraining needs ENE-labelled nodes we do not have. Treat as aspirational.

findings.title: Pretreatment Identification of Head and Neck Cancer Nodal Metastasis and Extranodal Extension Using Deep Learning Neural Networks (Kann et al., DualNet)
findings.summary: Original DualNet 3D CNN trained on annotated lymph node samples from pretreatment CT; AUC 0.91 for ENE and 0.91 for nodal metastasis on a held-out test set. Describes the node-crop preprocessing and the two-stream architecture used by all later ENE work.
findings.relevance: Open-access methods source if Margin ever trains its own ENE classifier; also the citation to show the surgeon-user when explaining what a radiologic-ENE score means and does not mean.
findings.license: Open access (CC BY) paper; weights not released
findings.feasibility: Small 3D CNN on a ~64^3 node patch - fully CPU-feasible if weights are obtained or retrained.

findings.title: Pretreatment CT Identification of Extranodal Extension in Laryngeal and Hypopharyngeal Cancers Using Deep Learning
findings.summary: Extends CT-based deep-learning ENE detection beyond oropharynx to laryngeal and hypopharyngeal primaries - the subsites where nodal ENE most changes surgical and adjuvant decisions. Most recent peer-reviewed validation of the Kann-style approach.
findings.relevance: Evidence that the ENE concept generalizes across the subsites a head & neck surgeon actually operates on; cite in Margin's ENE feature documentation and use to scope which primaries the feature should be offered for.
findings.license: Paywalled (RSNA)
findings.feasibility: No public weights located. Reference only.

findings.title: A Gradient Mapping Guided Explainable Deep Neural Network for Extracapsular Extension Identification in 3D Head and Neck Cancer CT Images
findings.summary: Explainable 3D DNN for extracapsular (extranodal) extension on CT that produces gradient-based saliency maps over the node, so the prediction can be inspected rather than taken on faith. Preprint with full architecture description.
findings.relevance: Directly relevant to Margin's design principle that a surgeon must be able to see WHY a flag fired. The saliency overlay maps cleanly onto a Cornerstone3D heatmap layer over the node crop.
findings.license: arXiv preprint; check for an associated code release before relying on it
findings.feasibility: Saliency/gradient maps need only a backward pass on a small patch - feasible on CPU in seconds.

findings.title: Automated Segmentation of Lymph Nodes on Neck CT Scans Using Deep Learning
findings.venue_or_repo: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine (PMC11612088), DOI 10.1007/s10278-024-01114-w
findings.summary: U-Net plus an adapted spatial-context network trained on 25,119 CT slices from 221 normal contrast-enhanced neck CTs (patients WITHOUT head and neck cancer), targeting small 5-10 mm nodes. Reported Dice 0.8084 for cervical node detection/segmentation.
findings.relevance: The node-finding half of Margin's node pipeline: detect nodes, then hand each one to the level-assignment step. Note the training set is normal necks, so sensitivity on grossly abnormal/necrotic nodes is unproven.
findings.license: Open access paper; no public weights found in this search
findings.feasibility: Largely 2D/slice-based, so CPU inference over a neck CT is minutes at worst - far cheaper than 3D-fullres nnU-Net.

findings.title: Automatic cervical lymph nodes detection and segmentation in heterogeneous computed tomography images using deep transfer learning
findings.summary: Transfer-learning approach to cervical node detection and segmentation explicitly designed for heterogeneous CT (varied scanners, protocols, contrast phases) rather than a single-institution protocol.
findings.relevance: Closest match to Margin's real input distribution - CTs from whatever outside facility the patient arrives with. Worth reading for the domain-robustness tricks (intensity harmonization, augmentation) to apply to any model we ship.
findings.license: Open access (Scientific Reports, CC BY); check the data/code availability statement for weights
findings.feasibility: Unverified; assume CPU-feasible only after checking the backbone size.

findings.title: TotalSegmentator - robust CT segmentation of >100 anatomical structures, including four head & neck subtasks
findings.summary: pip-installable nnU-Net-based tool. Free Apache-2.0 head & neck subtasks: head_glands_cavities (parotid, submandibular, pharyngeal structures, orbit), head_muscles (masseter, temporalis, pterygoids, tongue, digastric), headneck_bones_vessels (laryngeal cartilages, hyoid, carotids, jugulars), headneck_muscles (SCM, pharyngeal constrictors, scalenes, trapezius). brain_structures and face tasks require a separate non-commercial license.
findings.relevance: Gives Margin free anatomic context for essentially nothing: hyoid/cricoid/SCM/carotid/jugular landmarks are exactly the structures that define Robbins level boundaries, so this is both the fallback rule-based level engine AND the anatomy overlay for the Cornerstone3D viewer and for relating a tumor to at-risk structures.
findings.license: Apache-2.0 for code and the free tasks; brain_structures/face need a license from the author
findings.feasibility: Best-fit of everything here: explicitly supports Windows and CPU. pip install totalsegmentator. Use --fast (lower resolution) and --roi_subset to keep CPU runtime tolerable; the full 117-class head model wants ~20 GB for its forward pass, which 32 GB RAM can just handle but should be avoided - request only the ROIs needed.

findings.title: SegRap2023: A Benchmark of Organs-at-Risk and Gross Tumor Volume Segmentation for Radiotherapy Planning of Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
findings.venue_or_repo: arXiv / Medical Image Analysis; challenge at https://segrap2023.grand-challenge.org/
findings.summary: 400 CT scans from 200 NPC patients, each with paired pre-aligned non-contrast and contrast-enhanced CT; 45 OARs plus 2 GTVs (primary and nodal) annotated. One participating framework released at https://github.com/Astarakee/segrap2023.
findings.relevance: The only large public CT-ONLY (no PET) H&N tumor+OAR dataset with nodal GTV, which matches Margin's most common real input - a contrast neck CT with no PET. Use for training/validating a CT-only GTV model and for OAR context.
findings.license: Challenge DUA for the data; participant repo license must be checked on GitHub
findings.feasibility: Data download only. Training is GPU work and out of scope here; use it for validation of a downloaded model.

findings.title: Fully-automated, CT-only GTV contouring for palliative head and neck radiotherapy
findings.summary: nnU-Net trained on 102 non-contrast and 96 contrast-enhanced palliative H&N CTs across five strategies (heuristic crop, point-based crop, single vs separate GTV channels, synthetic-MR channel). Median Dice 0.6-0.7, surface Dice 0.30-0.56, HD95 14.7-19.7 mm.
findings.relevance: The honest performance ceiling for CT-ONLY GTV without PET - Dice ~0.65. Tells Margin to present CT-only auto-GTV as a draft contour a surgeon edits, never as a measurement, and shows that a single user click to seed the crop materially helps.
findings.license: Open access (Scientific Reports, CC BY); no public weights found
findings.feasibility: Reference. Confirms the point-prompt/crop pattern that makes CPU inference tractable (small crop instead of whole neck).

findings.title: nnInteractive - promptable 3D interactive segmentation (points, scribbles, boxes, lasso)
findings.summary: Trained on 120+ volumetric 3D datasets (CT, MRI, PET, microscopy); 2D interactions produce full 3D segmentations. Ships as nninteractive client/server pip packages and is already integrated into napari, MITK and a 3D Slicer extension.
findings.relevance: The most practical way for Margin to give a surgeon a usable tumor or node contour today: click the lesion in the Cornerstone3D viewer, get a 3D mask, compute volume. Sidesteps the absence of public H&N GTV weights entirely, because the surgeon supplies the localization.
findings.license: Code Apache-2.0; model checkpoint CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 - fine for Margin's local non-commercial use, blocks any commercial distribution
findings.feasibility: CAUTION: the authors state CPU is supported but slow, because it is 3D-convolution heavy, and they recommend a remote GPU. On an Intel iGPU box expect tens of seconds to minutes per prompt. Prototype it, measure real latency on a neck CT crop, and only ship it if a cropped ROI keeps it interactive.

findings.title: Determining the Optimal Prognostic Volumetric Threshold of Gross Tumor Volume in Head and Neck Cancer Treated by Radiotherapy
findings.venue_or_repo: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys (Red Journal)
findings.summary: Primary GTV <30 cc associated with markedly better outcomes: local control 100% vs 59.4%, nodal control 100% vs 66.8%, distant control 93.7% vs 69.4%, overall survival 93.1% vs 61.5%. Related ROC work supports GTV-P <30 cc, GTV-N <4 cc, GTV-P+N <50 cc as prognostic cutoffs.
findings.relevance: Turns Margin's volumetrics from a number into a decision aid: once a GTV mask exists (auto or surgeon-edited), report volume in cc against these thresholds. Cheapest high-value feature in this entire list - it is a voxel count times spacing.
findings.license: Paywalled journal article; cite only
findings.feasibility: Trivial. numpy sum of the mask times SimpleITK GetSpacing product. Microseconds, no model needed.

findings.title: External Validation of Pre-Treatment Primary Tumor Volume as a Prognostic Factor in Head and Neck Cancer Treated With (Chemo)Radiotherapy
findings.summary: Recent external validation that increasing primary tumor volume (GTVp) predicts local failure and worse progression-free and overall survival, retaining significance on multivariable analysis adjusted for stage, subsite and race. Reported in a large oropharyngeal SCC cohort (~1286 patients in related analyses).
findings.relevance: The modern citation that justifies showing tumor volume as a prognostic biomarker in Margin rather than as a curiosity - and evidence that it adds information beyond T stage, which is the argument for putting it in a surgeon's pre-op summary.
findings.license: Paywalled (Wiley); cite only
findings.feasibility: No compute. Pairs with the volumetrics computation above.

findings.title: Preoperative Determination of Depth of Invasion in Oral Cavity Squamous Cell Carcinoma by Standard Cross-Sectional Imaging With CT and PET/CT
findings.summary: Assesses how well routine CT and PET/CT estimate pathologic depth of invasion in oral cavity SCC - the measurement that drives T stage and the elective neck dissection decision under AJCC 8.
findings.relevance: Core to a Margin 'measure DOI on this axial/coronal slice' tool: defines what a radiologic DOI measurement is worth and what to warn the surgeon about when it drives elective neck management.
findings.license: Open access (PMC)
findings.feasibility: Pure viewer feature - a perpendicular-from-mucosal-surface caliper in Cornerstone3D. No model, no GPU.

findings.title: Measurement variations of MRI and CT in the assessment of tumor depth of invasion in oral cancer
findings.summary: CT and MRI systematically OVERESTIMATE histologic DOI in oral SCC, especially for tumors with DOI <5 mm, producing imaging upstaging in over 50% of cases; artifacts degraded more than 20% of studies. Related MRI work suggests shifted imaging cutoffs (~6.2 mm and ~11.4 mm) to match pathologic 5 mm and 10 mm.
findings.relevance: The single most important safety caveat for a Margin DOI tool. If Margin reports radiologic DOI it must display the overestimation bias and the shifted cutoffs, or it will push surgeons toward unnecessary elective neck dissections in thin tumors.
findings.license: Paywalled (Elsevier); cite only
findings.feasibility: No compute. Implement as a calibration note plus optional shifted-threshold display in the UI.

findings.title: Deep Learning Based HPV Status Prediction for Oropharyngeal Cancer Patients
findings.summary: 3D convolutional network pretrained on sports video clips, fine-tuned on CT crops around oropharyngeal tumors; AUC 0.81 on an external test set. One of the earliest credible CT-only HPV classifiers.
findings.relevance: Upper-bound reference for a Margin HPV feature. Read alongside HECKTOR 2025's 0.56 balanced accuracy - single-center AUCs near 0.8 do not survive multi-center testing, which is the reason to skip this feature.
findings.license: arXiv preprint; no public weights located
findings.feasibility: Small 3D CNN on a tumor crop - CPU-feasible if weights existed.

findings.title: Human papillomavirus (HPV) prediction for oropharyngeal cancer based on CT using off-the-shelf features: a dual-dataset study
findings.venue_or_repo: Medical Physics / J Appl Clin Med Phys (PMC12059277)
findings.summary: Combines radiomics and off-the-shelf deep features across two datasets; the paper states source code, radiomics and deep features, and statistical-analysis data are publicly available. Reported AUC ~0.79 (95% CI 0.781-0.809) with average recall 0.827 in the related I3D/SlowFast formulation.
findings.relevance: The one HPV study in this search with a stated public code release, so it is the only realistic route if Margin ever revisits HPV-from-CT. Its radiomics pipeline (pyradiomics on a GTV mask) is CPU-trivial and reusable for other endpoints.
findings.license: Open access paper; verify the repository license in the data-availability statement
findings.feasibility: pyradiomics pip-installs and runs on CPU in seconds per lesion; the classifier is scikit-learn scale. Fully feasible - the blocker is evidence quality, not compute.

findings.title: nnU-Net v2 for Head-and-Neck PET/CT Primary Tumor and Lymph Node Segmentation: A Simple, Strong Baseline (HECKTOR 2025)
findings.summary: Shows an out-of-the-box nnU-Net v2 configuration remains a top-tier baseline for joint GTVp/GTVn segmentation on PET/CT, competitive with bespoke architectures in the 2025 challenge.
findings.relevance: Argues Margin should not chase exotic architectures: standardize on nnU-Net v2, which is the same runtime already needed for the lymph-node-level weights. One inference stack, two models.
findings.license: Paywalled chapter; nnU-Net itself is Apache-2.0
findings.feasibility: Single shared nnU-Net v2 CPU runtime for both the nodal-level model and any GTV model keeps the Python dependency surface small - important on a locked-down Windows box behind a proxy.

gaps: No publicly released weights for any CT-only or PET/CT H&N GTV segmentation model were found. Every challenge winner published methods, not checkpoints. Margin either retrains (needs GPU we do not have), uses interactive segmentation (nnInteractive), or ships no auto-GTV.
No public weights or code for any ENE classifier (Kann JCO 2020, Kann Sci Rep 2018, Radiology 2025). A radiologic-ENE feature is currently not implementable locally.

The one strong asset with permissive licensing - the CC0 lymph node LEVEL weights - was trained on 35 radiotherapy PLANNING CTs (arms-down, specific protocol). Its behavior on diagnostic neck CTs with contrast and on post-operative/post-radiation necks is unvalidated and must be tested before a surgeon trusts a level label.

CPU latency is unmeasured for every model here. nnU-Net 3D-fullres and nnInteractive are both explicitly flagged as slow on CPU. Margin needs a real benchmark on the Intel iGPU box before committing to an interactive UX; consider OpenVINO or ONNX Runtime export as a mitigation (not researched here).
No model detects lymph node NECROSIS, matting, or the specific CT signs a surgeon actually uses; published node models segment nodes or predict ENE as a black box.
No automatic DOI-from-imaging model exists - all DOI literature is manual measurement plus correction factors. This is a viewer/measurement feature, not an AI feature.

Robbins nomenclature vs the Gregoire/DAHANCA level nomenclature are not identical (Gregoire adds levels and renames boundaries). A mapping table between the 20 released model labels, Gregoire levels, and surgical Robbins levels must be hand-authored and verified by the surgeon-author.
Licensing of the HNLNL release binaries was confirmed only at the repository level (CC0-1.0). Confirm the release assets carry the same terms before bundling them into a distributable Margin build.
No investigation of DICOM RTSTRUCT/SEG round-tripping, which Margin will need to export any of these masks back to a PACS or planning system.
